sources.title: PlayStation Cancels Live-Service Heist Shooter, Fairgames
sources.text: Fairgames , a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony. A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Fairgames has been scrapped, three and a half years after its announcement. Developer Haven Studios will not be shut down, nor will there be any layoffs, as PlayStation has decided to turn the team into a support studio for other first-party projects. The decision to pull the plug on the game was made after a recent test did not meet internal expectations. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” said executives Sean Decker and John Doyle in a note reviewed by Bloomberg. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” The test being referenced here is likely one that made some waves earlier this fall. A mysterious game known as Project Espresso, which looked a lot like Fairgames, began advertising private playtests with a gameplay trailer back in September . Not much is known about those tests, but they didn't seem to be very fruitful for the team. Fairgames was announced in 2023 and has been the subject of scrutiny for some time. Some fans pushed back on PlayStation's live-service pivot during the early 2020s, as the company has always excelled with blockbuster single-player games. When Concord bombed , fans began to express even further revulsion toward titles like Fairgames. The project has also been soured by a number of setbacks, including departures of key developers and internal struggles . Fairgames' cancelation marks yet another major failure for PlayStation's live-service efforts. Concord flopped, The Last of Us Online was scrapped , an online God of War game was killed , and Marathon has been struggling since launch. Helldivers 2, on the other hand, has been a big win for PlayStation. There's some hope that maybe Bungie's decision to revive Destiny 2 could be productive , but Sony seems to be moving away from live-service. The only other major live-service game from PlayStation on the horizon is 4:Loop , a new game from JJ Abrams' studio, Bad Robot. We'll see if it suffers a similar fate as these other titles. Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

sources.text: Sony has canceled Fairgames (stylized as FairGame$), the upcoming live-service shooter from Haven Studios, according to Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier. The decision brings an end to a project that was first announced in 2023 as part of PlayStation’s push into the live-service market. The game had been in development for several years and underwent multiple reworks, with the studio even planning a re-reveal under a new title. According to Bloomberg , a recent playtest involving thousands of players failed to meet Sony’s expectations. While the test demonstrated strong technical performance and live-service readiness, player feedback and retention numbers were mixed. Insider Gaming first reported back in April that the game was struggling to “find the fun” in pre-alpha tests. Despite multiple changes to the game, including a likely name change to “Break In” and a move towards the extraction shooter genre, the game never got off the ground internally. In an internal email to employees, PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle explained the decision to stop development. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” the executives wrote. They also pointed to challenging market conditions in the player-versus-player shooter genre as another factor behind the cancellation. Despite the decision, Sony confirmed that there will be no job cuts at Haven Studios as a result. Instead, the Montreal-based developer will shift its focus toward supporting other studios within PlayStation. Fairgames was one of several live-service projects Sony had pursued as part of its broader strategy to expand beyond traditional single-player experiences. That strategy has faced several setbacks, with the company reassessing its approach to live-service development. The cancellation marks another major change for Haven Studios, which Sony acquired in 2022. It remains to be seen what projects the studio will support moving forward. sources.text: After a long development, it’s being reported that Fairgames is no more PlayStation has reportedly cancelled its upcoming live service game, Fairgames. As reported by Bloomberg , PlayStation says it cancelled Fairgames after the results of a recent playtest “fell short of the goals we had set.” It comes three years after Fairgames was initially revealed in 2023. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” reads a note reportedly penned by executives Sean Decker and John Doyle. âCombined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” Footage from this playtest seemingly leaked online in September . If this was indeed Fairgames, then it was the first piece of gameplay footage we had seen. Other than that, all we had to go on were cinematics in the announcement trailer from 2023. It is being reported that developer Haven Studios will not be closing down as a result of this decision, nor will there be any layoffs. This also comes as Sony ‘s live service ventures have produced mixed results. While Helldivers 2 was a win, Concord flopped, and PlayStation went on to shut down developer Firewalk Studios. Meanwhile, Bungie is trying to grow Marathon ‘s playerbase, so it makes sense that PlayStation doesn’t want to add another live service into the mix right now. With these factors in mind, this report regarding Fairgames is unsurprising. We already knew that development was struggling behind the scenes, as it had been reported that internal playtests were negatively received as far back as 2025. If recent playtests failed to inspire either, it’s likely Sony decided not to fund the project further, especially given the state of the live service market. PlayStation is yet to publicly comment on claims that Fairgames has been cancelled.

sources.text: Sony's latest game cancellation adds to a long list of failed GaaS projects Sony has canceled Fairgames (aka Fairgame$ ) three years after the live-service shooter was announced, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday. No one at its developer, Haven Studios, is getting laid off, and instead Haven will support other Sony Interactive Entertainment-owned studios, according to that report. Farigames recently held a playtest and, according to an internal email reviewed by Bloomberg, feedback from that playtest didn't live up to PlayStation's expectations. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in the email. With "challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre," Sony decided to cancel the game. Fairgames reportedly had been reworked multiple times since its 2023 reveal. It would have been the debut game from Haven, which was founded in 2021 by former Assassin's Creed producer and Google Stadia Games and Entertainment head Jade Raymond , who has since left the studio. Haven was acquired by Sony in 2022 . Back in 2022, Sony announced a huge push for live-service games , aiming to release at least 10 by 2026. While games like Helldivers 2 and Gran Turismo 7 have been steady live-service hits, Sony's push has largely failed. Concord is the most notable misfire , as it was actually released before Sony reversed course and shut it down shortly after launch in embarrassing fashion. A live-service God of War game , a multiplayer The Last of Us game , and many others were canceled before they could see the light of day. PlayStation studios working on live-service games, including London Studios, Firewalk Studios, and Bluepoint Games, were all shut down in recent years. In June, Sony laid off most of the Destiny team at Bungie, as " Destiny 2 fell short of expectations" with players. Recently, Horizon Hunters Gathering was reportedly delayed so it can be rebooted in response to negative player feedback (which sounds not too dissimilar to the Fairgames situation).

sources.text: Fairgames was revealed in 2023, but nothing more was ever seen of it. A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023 , has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia , Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios , which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation." In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world. But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release . Of the remaining games, one was Marathon , which endures but has not lived up to expectations, and another was Concord , one of the most famously disastrous game launches in years, which was taken offline less than two weeks after it launched, never to return. A live-service spinoff of the Horizon series, Hunters Gathering, was also reportedly rebooted after negative feedback from playtests . A partial accounting of canned multiplayer projects: The Concord catastrophe in particular seemed to shake Sony, which began reversing its live service strategy just a few months later. Fairgames itself looked to be in trouble in 2025 when Raymond departed Haven , reportedly after an external playtest left PlayStation leadership "concerned about how the game was received and its progress." The Bloomberg report says a more recent large-scale playtest produced similar results. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email sent to Haven Studios employees. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." The one bright spot to the cancellation is that no jobs will be cut because of it: A Sony rep told Bloomberg that Haven "will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." sources.title: PlayStation adds live-service shooter Fairgames to its constantly expanding graveyard
sources.text: Sony's trail of bodies is only getting longer Sony has dug up another plot in its expanding live-service graveyard, and is lowering the still-warm corpse of Haven Studios' Fairgames into the dirt. The shooter, which was revealed in 2023, has been canceled, though PlayStation says there will be no layoffs as a result of its decision to end the project. "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities," a PlayStation representative tells Bloomberg , who first reported the news. Fairgames was revealed in a 2023 trailer which stylized the title as "Fairgame$." The trailer featured no in-game footage, but presented a stylish version of a Payday-style shooter focused on heists. But the game never materialized again. The last major news on the project came in 2025, when Haven Studios founder Jade Raymond – a veteran Ubisoft producer who'd worked on Assassins' Creed – left the company . Bloomberg reports that Fairgames was ultimately canceled after a poor showing during a recent test session with thousands of players. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," according to an internal memo. PlayStation had apparently reworked the game multiple times since it was first revealed, and prior to the test had planned to showcase it again under a new title, according to the report. While PlayStation once had extensive plans for live-service games, it's canceled so many of those projects that it's now difficult to keep track of them all. The death of Concord just two weeks after launch is perhaps the highest profile example, but that's just the most memorable corpse among an extensive trail of bodies. A multiplayer God of War title from Bluepoint and a live-service game from Bend Studio were canceled in 2025 . A multitude of unannounced projects were iced amid mass layoffs at PlayStation in 2024, including a Twisted Metal game and an original project from the publisher's now-defunct London studio. Naughty Dog 's The Last of Us multiplayer game died in 2023 . Bungie has reportedly had numerous projects scrapped since it was acquired by Sony. PlayStation has even killed not just one , but two projects helmed by Call of Duty veteran Jason Blundell. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Sony's biggest live-service hit in recent years is certainly Helldivers 2, but it's struggled to replicate that success – heck, it's struggled to release other online games at any scale. The publisher's annual MLB The Show series remains a staple among baseball fans, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls seems to have found a niche among fighting game aficionados, and Marathon is continuing to survive, but these aren't the Fortnite-level hits Sony is clearly gunning for. I guess we'll never know whether Fairgames could've been a hit. sources.title: How to unlock Fire Arrows in Zelda Ocarina of Time
sources.text: Unlocking Fire Arrows is a great way to expand Link's arsenal in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. By hitting targets with these special arrows, Link can set them on fire, which is fairly useful in different scenarios, from fighting certain enemies to lighting totems to open doors. Before you can get your hands on them, you will need to progress through the story and solve a riddle. If you need help figuring out all the steps, don't fret. Here's how to unlock Fire Arrows in Zelda Ocarina of Time . Before you start shooting Fire Arrows around Hyrule, you need to meet two prerequisites : get the Fairy Bow from the Forest Temple and complete the Water Temple in Lake Hylia. If you have already finished the Water Temple, head to the largest island in the middle of the lake (the one with the large tree) and read the tablet located on the its southeast side. The message says, "When the lake is full and dawn breaks, release an arrow toward the halo of light," which basically means that you need to shoot an arrow at the sun . Wait until daytime and aim your bow at the rising sun . If you're visiting the lake during the night, you can use the Sun's Song to speed the process up. As you aim your bow at the sun, an orange-reddish circle will appear around it , indicating that you should fire the arrow. A short cutscene will play, showing the arrow landing on the island in front of you. Head there and pick up the Fire Arrow. When it comes to using Fire Arrows, it's important to keep in mind that they aren't a separate type of arrow. What you unlock is the ability to magically imbue your arrows with fire . While this means you won't have to carry a stock of each type, it also means that you have only one set of arrows to use, whether you're shooting regular or Fire Arrows. Additionally, Fire Arrows cost one magic power per shot, considerably limiting the number of times you can use them. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a little bit different than the original game, so if you need guides to help you through, we don’t blame you. We have walkthroughs for all the dungeons, from the Deku Tree to Ganondorf's Castle . We also have guides for the sillier, in-between parts of the game, like when you have to find Richard (the dog) or Cuccos . For those going for 100% completion, we also have guides on where to find every Piece of Heart , every Gold Skulltula token , and where to plant every Magic Bean .

sources.text: Nintendo Switch 2 The Legend of Zelda The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Well, you’ve made it. You’re finally at the most infamous dungeon in all of Zelda -dom, the Water Temple of Ocarina of Time . Good news for you: In the remake, this dungeon is far, far easier than it’s ever been. A few of the edges have been sanded down, the rooms all look far more distinct and memorable so it’s less of a mental maze, and the iron boots can be equipped and de-equipped simply by pressing down on the gamepad. Compared to the original, it’s a smooth ride. But still, this is one of the most involved dungeons in the game, so buckle on that Zora Tunic and let’s get swimming. To enter the Water Temple, you need to be wearing (no, I wasn’t joking) the Zora Tunic, which you get by freeing King Zora from his ice block back in Zora Domain. To do that, you need Blue Fire in a bottle, which you obtain in the Ice Cavern as an adult. You’ll also need the Iron Boots from that same cavern. If you haven’t gotten that far yet, back yourself up and come back to this guide later. Once you’re in the temple, remove your iron boots and float to the top. Run forward, and you’ll be in a big, open room with a bunch of doors on all four sides across four different floors, and water below you. I’m going to be referring to this as the “main hall” going forward. We’re going to be here a lot. I’ll also be referring to doors by floor and cardinal direction, so if you’re ever confused about what I’m talking about, open that map. The first thing you’re going to do is slay that Blue Tektite in front of you. Sword, hookshot, whatever you like, just get it out of the way. Next, you’re going to equip those Iron Boots, descend to the first floor, and head through the east door. Once you’re inside, remove the boots to float upward for a cutscene with your fiancee, Ruto. When it’s over, grab the Dungeon Map from the chest in front of you, and then stand on the platform with the Triforce symbol and play Zelda’s Lullaby to lower the water level. Real quick tip: There are three different spots to mess with the water level in this dungeon, and each one will raise it to a different spot. This one brings it down to the first floor, and is marked by glowy blue pillars. It might be good to make a note somewhere of which color results in which water level, just in case you ever get turned around or confused and the water level is in the wrong place. Once the water has dropped, fearlessly jump down the hole, landing in the water below so it doesn’t damage you. Now, with the water taken care of, note that one of the torches in here is lit. Stand behind it with your bow equipped and aim an arrow through the fire to each of the two torches on the other end of the room to open the door in front of you, then enter. Defeat the three Spikes by blocking their attacks with your shield and swinging your sword when they’re vulnerable to obtain a Small Key. (Din’s Fire is also usable for this puzzle). Backtrack the way you came in and head out into the main hall. There are two more aptly named Spikes out here waiting for you; get rid of them. To your left (west side, 1F) is a bombable/breakable wall. Knock that out, and use your Iron Boots to sink, sink, sink. Head down the underwater corridor and take care of the Shell Blade by hitting it with your hookshot when its mouth is all the way open. At the end of the corridor, take off the boots and rise up. In here, climb the platform jutting out of the water and use the hookshot to grapple onto the pillars ahead of you. Take down the Tektites and the Like Like (Hookshot is great here), and you’ll be rewarded with the Compass. Now, all the way back to the main hall! To the west (1F) is a block you can push forward until it drops in the water. Do that, then use the boots to sink again. Look out for the Shell Blade in the way, then rise back up at the end of the hall. You’ll find yourself in a room with a whirlpool and some statues underwater, and a chest on the other side. This looks trickier than it is. Use the iron boots to drop into the whirlpool, aiming for the center platform (the serpent’s body) stretched down the middle of the pool. Stand on the platform and use your hookshot to smack the weird gem thing in the serpent’s mouth. This will unlock the underwater grate, allowing you to enter. You might need to don and doff the iron boots a few times to swim over properly, but with some careful aiming it’s very doable. There are two more Shell Blades to fight inside, after which you’re free to take off the boots, rise to the surface, and grab the small key. Back across the whirlpool, out the door, into the main hall again. There’s a locked door on the central pillar here, directly in front of you, and you now have a key. Head inside. Once inside, step forward, turn around, and look up for a grapple point. Use your hookshot to get on the platform above. Right in front of you is a spot to stand and play Zelda’s Lullaby to raise the water back up. ( Note : the columns here are green, green brings the water to 2F! Write it down if you need to!) Before you leave this inside pillar, though, jump in the water and look down: a new gap has opened up with the water level rising. Use iron boots to drop down, where three Spikes are waiting for you. Kill them with the hookshot, then use the hookshot to hit the green switch above your head, releasing a Shell Blade. Kill that too, then remove the iron boots where it was standing to rise up into the now-open area. There’s a red rupee in a chest on the way up, as well as a gold skulltula on the wall opposite. sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake removed Mario and Skyward Sword references to not "interrupt" players
sources.text: Thankfully, Skyward Sword's director says "no hard feelings" The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is, by most standards, a pretty faithful remake to the original game, but Nintendo wasn't scared to make changes where necessary. I was a little bummed to learn the fun references to the Super Mario Bros. series had been removed, not to mention some Zelda: Skyward Sword art that was in the Ocarina of Time 3DS remake, but with how carefully Nintendo positions every game, remaster, and remake into its existing portfolio, I'm not at all surprised. In case you aren't a Zelda historian, the original game has several Mario references including character portraits and heavy design influences on characters like Talon, Malon, and Ingo, who strongly resemble Mario, Peach, and Luigi, respectively. It makes a lot of sense as Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Super Mario 64 were both being made at the same time, but 30 years later, the remake doesn't share that same connection to Mario 64. That's why the portraits have been removed from the remake, even though it's still pretty clear Talon, Malon, and Ingo have doppelgangers hanging out in the Mario universe. "Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal. Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing," Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma tells Game Informer . "But looking at it now, like if a player is coming through that area, and given the overall way that we're, you know, creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time." Similarly to the original Ocarina of Time and Mario 64, 3DS Ocarina of Time released around the same time as Zelda: Skyward Sword, which explains the crossover references there. And likewise, they were removed from the new Ocarina of Time remake so as not to distract from everything else going on. "I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game, and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that. So I said, 'Okay, sure,'" says Aonuma, but same as before with the Mario 64 references, "you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way." Game Informer was kind enough to consider the feelings of Skyward Sword director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, who took part in the same interview, but thankfully it's all water under the bridge. "It's really as Mr. Aonuma said. There was an underlying concept in what we were going for, so no hard feelings there," he says. sources.title: Which Dog is Richard in Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake?
sources.text: The Richard the Dog sequence in The Legend of Zelda : Ocarina of Time is an iconic part of the original game. In this quest, Link must help Richard’s owner locate the missing dog who is roaming the streets of Hyrule Castle Town during the night. This activity is back again in the Ocarina of Time Remake, but the location of both Richard and his owner have been totally changed this time around. Since this isn’t a sequence you’ll automatically have the solution for even as a longtime OOT fan, let’s lay out exactly how to find and return Richard in the new remake. Completing the Richard quest isn’t available the first time you reach Hyrule Castle Town. Here’s everything you must do before Richard goes missing: It’s unclear why getting Death Mountain Trail access is the trigger for Richard to run away from his owner, but regardless, these steps must be followed first. The first time you arrive in Hyrule Castle Town before you’ve met Princess Zelda, the game doesn’t allow time of day to progress to nightfall, which is when Richard goes missing. However, even after your introduction to Zelda, if you immediately return to Hyrule Castle Town at night, Richard still won’t run away. Instead, you’ll just be able to observe Richard and his owner repeatedly hanging out in the Market, then returning home together when the sun sets. Once you have Zelda’s letter, head straight to the guard standing by the large, shut gate in Kakariko Village who is preventing you from accessing Death Mountain Trail. Present Zelda’s letter to the guard to open the gate. For whatever reason, after this is done, Richard will now be missing the next time you return to Hyrule Castle Town after dark. As an added tip, and since you’re already in Kakariko Village anyway, consider stopping by the Graveyard in order to obtain the Sun’s Song from the Royal Family Tomb (unlocked by playing Zelda’s Lullaby directly in front of the giant headstone in the back of the cemetery). The Sun’s Song is a huge quality-of-life ocarina tune in the game anyway, and you can use it for the Richard quest to make sure you’re entering Hyrule Castle Town at night. After meeting the prerequisites and returning to the market at night, you’ll find Richard’s owner outside of a building to the right, just before the entrance to the large market square. She’ll let you know Richard has gone missing, which is your cue to spring into action. In the original game, Richard was hanging out behind the fruit stand outside the bazaar, but that’s not the case in the remake. Instead, head to the back alley, coincidentally close to Richard’s actual house. But there’s one other issue to sort out; you’ll actually notice two white dogs in the back alley, making it tough to know which one is actually Richard. Visually, these two white dogs look identical. The trick here is to use the “Play” prompt when you stand next to one of the dogs and listen to the pitches of their barks. Richard has a very high-pitched bark, while the imposter dog has a very low one. Richard is also the one who runs around directly in front of the Treasure Chest Game, which has also been relocated to the back alley. “Play” with the higher-pitched white dog, which will trigger him to follow you around. Return him to his concerned owner, and your good deed is complete. For rescuing Richard and returning him, his owner will bestow a shiny heart piece upon you for your troubles. Right after this, Richard runs off again. Don’t worry about it, however. I tried to see if there were any secondary rewards for returning Richard multiple times, and there are not. In fact, though he runs off again immediately, it’s actually because he’s now returning to his home in the back alley. How do you feel about these little tweaks the remake has switched up in Zelda: Ocarina of Time? Be sure to let us know in the Insider Gaming Discord server . Looking for more Zelda talk? Check out our full review of the Ocarina of Time Remake . For more gaming news and stories delivered directly to you, be sure to subscribe to the Insider Gaming newsletter . sources.text: November’s lineup of games on PlayStation Plus has been revealed by Sony. Ahead of the holiday season, PlayStation Plus members are getting a wide variety of free games that they can try out on the service, including two big titles from Kojima Productions and Ryu Ga Gotoku. The first game on this list is Death Stranding 2: On the Beach . The sequel to the first Death Stranding game, this follow-up takes eleven months after the events of its predecessor, featuring Sam Porter Bridges and Fragile as they set out across Australia to connect surviving colonies with the Chiral Network. It’s well worth a play, especially with this deal on PS Plus; in our review, IGN’s Simon Cardy scored the game a 9 out of 10 , calling it a “triumphant sequel that emphatically delivers on the promise of its original.” Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii is the second game on this month’s list. Join an amnesiac Goro Majima after he wakes up stranded on an island, gather a crew of pirates, and uncover a hidden treasure in this spinoff of the Yakuza series. It’s a delightfully fun romp, and another title that’s well worth taking advantage of if you’re a PS Plus subscriber; IGN’s Tristan Ogilvie scored the game an 8 out of 10 in our review , calling it “a consistently captivating voyage that kept my timbers shivering whether on land or at sea.” Other games included in this month’s PS Plus lineup are Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake , a reimagining of the beloved classic that earned a 9 out of 10 from our reviewer, as well as 2025 survival-action game Atomfall , first-person shooter Trepang2 , and racing game MotoGP 26 . sources.text: Death Stranding 2! Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii! Atomfall! Sony's revealed the second wave of games coming to PlayStation Plus Premium and Extra this month, and there are some genuine big-name attractions, led by Hideo Kojima 's futuristic delivery man showstopper Death Stranding 2: On the Beach . Here's the new games coming PlayStation Plus Extra and Premium in November: And here are a couple of games coming only to PlayStation Plus Premium in November: There's a lot to recommend in that list. Death Stranding 2 was one of the standout games of 2025. "A busier, louder, and more emotionally resplendent take on this singular hiking sim," Lewis Gordon wrote in Eurogamer's Death Stranding 2 review . Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii also shone brightly last year, as ridiculous as it was. "A raucous, absurd spin-off that manages to still feel like a first-rate Yakuza game despite the leftfield setting and delightfully unhinged plot," wrote Matt Elliott in Eurogamer's Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii review . Meanwhile, Atomfall - Rebellion's quirky British take on a Fallout-like post-apocalyptic idea - was awarded three out of five stars. "If you can get over a difficult start and fancy a lean take on the survival genre, Atomfall delivers an intriguing tale worth discovering," Tom Orry wrote in Eurogamer's Atomfall review . It's presumably been significantly patched and smoothed since then. The Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake also scored three out of five stars. "Some excellent enhancements make this the ultimate version of Dragon Quest 3, but it could still do more to make it wholly welcoming to newcomers," Daniella Lucas wrote in Eurogamer's Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D review . We didn't review Hell Let Loose, but the popular World War 2 shooter would go on to amass a serious following and spawn a follow-up game in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam recently, which we did review . "The lavish jungles, rigid command structure, and emphasis on communication make Hell Let Loose: Vietnam a fascinating war simulator when it works. But its many variables can all too easily devolve into a miserable snipe-fest," Rick Lane wrote. There's plenty to be getting on with, then. Sony also announced in the PlayStation Blog post it's retiring the PS Plus app on PC from 10th December. Why? Because nobody really uses it. "With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4 percent) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use," Sony wrote. "As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available." sources.text: Rockstar also says GTA 6 will play best on PS5 Rockstar has finally confirmed that Grand Theft Auto 6 will target 30 FPS on all platforms. In a statement, Rockstar outlines what performance we can expect across PlayStation and Xbox consoles. The big takeaway here is that we’ll be playing at 30 FPS, and ray-tracing will be limited to PS5 Pro. “ Grand Theft Auto 6 has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life â while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants,” the statement reads. “The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro.” Rockstar also repeats the claim that GTA 6 will “play best on PlayStation 5 consoles”. “Grand Theft Auto 6 for PS5 includes high-fidelity haptic feedback fully integrated across the game on DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial audio rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D Audio, and improved load times,” Rockstar says. As for Xbox, GTA 6 will actually be playable on Xbox One via cloud streaming, “utilising Xbox Series S graphics settings”.Â Furthermore, Remote Play will be supported on PlayStation and Xbox. Lastly, we just got a new trailer, although it doesn’t give too much away. This announcement comes as pre-loading goes live across both platforms. This allows everyone to pre-install the game so they can play GTA 6 as soon as it launches on November 19. Rockstar is on track for a huge launch, with pre-orders exceeding Take-Two’s expectations . That is despite pushback against the decision to release GTA 6 without a physical copy . It will be the first mainline game in the series to be digital-only, around the same time that PlayStation announced that it is phasing out physical game releases on its platforms by 2028 .

sources.text: Rockstar divulga trailer de lançamento de GTA 6! Assista novo vídeo legendado em PT-BR A Rockstar confirmou que GTA 6 terá como alvo 30 FPS no PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. Em comunicado divulgado nesta terça (10), a desenvolvedora também revelou que o ray tracing será um recurso exclusivo do PS5 Pro — que terá melhorias visuais em relação aos demais aparelhos. Segundo a empresa, o jogo foi desenvolvido para aproveitar ao máximo o hardware da atual geração, priorizando a qualidade gráfica e a densidade do mundo aberto. A confirmação reforça uma declaração feita em agosto por Rob Nelson, chefe de desenvolvimento e co-diretor da Rockstar North, que já havia mencionado os 30 quadros por segundo durante a produção . Na ocasião, o executivo explicou que a equipe ainda precisava avaliar a possibilidade de oferecer 60 FPS no lançamento ou em uma atualização futura. Agora, a Rockstar voltou a destacar que a prioridade é manter a fidelidade visual e o desempenho previsto para os consoles. Em comunicado, a Rockstar explicou que GTA 6 foi desenvolvido do zero para os consoles atuais, com meta de 30 FPS. A empresa afirma que o objetivo é manter a qualidade visual e a densidade dos ambientes e personagens de Leonida. “ Grand Theft Auto 6 foi totalmente desenvolvido do zero para proporcionar a melhor experiência possível para a geração atual de consoles, visando 30 quadros por segundo e levando ambas as plataformas ao seu limite absoluto”, declarou a desenvolvedora. O PS5 Pro terá recursos visuais adicionais, incluindo melhorias de nitidez por meio da tecnologia PSSR e sombras com ray tracing. Segundo a Rockstar, essas funcionalidades serão exclusivas do console mais potente da Sony. A empresa também voltou a afirmar que GTA 6 terá sua melhor experiência nos consoles PlayStation 5. No Xbox, o jogo poderá ser acessado pelo Xbox Cloud Gaming e utilizará as configurações gráficas da versão para Series S. O Remote Play também será compatível com os consoles das duas fabricantes. A decisão de manter GTA 6 a 30 FPS segue um padrão dos jogos recentes de mundo aberto da Rockstar. GTA 5 , por exemplo, só recebeu suporte a 60 quadros por segundo nos consoles com suas versões para PS5 e Xbox Series X|S. Já Red Dead Redemption 2 continua limitado a 30 FPS nos consoles atuais e ainda não recebeu uma versão nativa de nova geração com uma taxa de quadros maior. O primeiro Red Dead Redemption , por outro lado, recebeu versões recentes com suporte a 60 quadros por segundo. Até o momento, a Rockstar não anunciou uma versão de GTA 6 para PC. A empresa costuma lançar seus jogos inicialmente nos consoles e disponibilizar uma edição para computadores posteriormente, geralmente com opções adicionais de desempenho e configurações gráficas. Lembrando que a Rockstar também liberou o pré-carregamento de GTA 6 nesta terça-feira (10) no PS5 e no Xbox Series X|S. A função permite baixar os arquivos do jogo antecipadamente para que os jogadores possam começar a aventura assim que o título for lançado, em 19 de novembro. Quem comprou o jogo digitalmente pode configurar o console para realizar o download automático. No PS5, é necessário ativar os downloads automáticos e deixar o aparelho ligado ou em modo de repouso. No Xbox, basta habilitar as atualizações automáticas e manter o console ligado ou em suspensão. A PlayStation recomenda reservar pelo menos 212 GB de espaço livre no armazenamento do PS5 para instalar o jogo. O acesso será liberado à meia-noite de 19 de novembro, conforme o horário local de cada região. sources.text: The day has come: if you’ve preordered Grand Theft Auto 6 , you can now preload the game onto your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. Na indústria de games, isso significa que a versão final destinada à distribuição foi oficialmente concluída e a etapa principal de desenvolvimento chegou ao fim. Normalmente, o anúncio de que um jogo atingiu esse estágio acontece semanas antes do lançamento, já que as empresas precisam preparar cópias físicas, embalagens e a distribuição para lojas — mesmo que o conteúdo da mídia física seja apenas um código digital. “Neste momento, a Rockstar concluiu o desenvolvimento de GTA 6”, confirmou Zelnick na teleconferência de resultados da última segunda (09), reiterando que a Rockstar fez “o seu melhor trabalho até agora”. Como a distribuição digital não depende do envio de discos para fábricas, a Rockstar pode concentrar os preparativos na versão digital e na infraestrutura da PlayStation Network. Informações sobre os arquivos hospedados na rede da Sony também indicam que a estrutura de distribuição do jogo já está preparada. O status Gold, no entanto, não significa que todo o trabalho terminou. A equipe ainda pode desenvolver uma atualização de primeiro dia, realizar testes nos servidores e corrigir possíveis problemas antes da estreia. Além disso, o marco não elimina completamente a possibilidade de mudanças no cronograma de lançamento. Vale lembrar também que o pré-carregamento de GTA 6 já começou no PS5 e no Xbox Series X|S , permitindo que os jogadores baixem os arquivos antes da estreia. sources.text: Soul Reaver 2 e Freedom Wars Remastered entram no PlayStation Plus Deluxe. Neste mês, embarque em uma missão inspiradora de conexão humana em Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, reúna uma tripulação única enquanto navega o alto-mar em Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii, explore ruínas controladas por seitas, cavernas naturais e bunkers nucleares de uma zona rural britânica inóspita e coberta de vegetação em Atomfall, ou explore um vasto mapa repleto de locais cativantes em Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake. Todos esses títulos e muitos outros estão disponíveis na seleção de novembro do Catálogo de jogos do PlayStation Plus *. Enquanto isso, Soul Reaver 2 e Freedom Wars Remastered chegam ao PlayStation Plus Deluxe. Embarque em uma missão inspiradora de conexão humana que vai além da UCA. Acompanhe Sam no próximo capítulo de sua jornada, enquanto ele tenta conectar a Austrália à Rede Quiral. Explore um ambiente natural passando por ciclos diurnos e noturnos, além de desastres naturais, incluindo terremotos, tempestades de areia e incêndios florestais, e a Chuva temporal, uma chuva que envelhece instantaneamente tudo o que toca. Para atravessar esta paisagem perigosa, você precisará construir novos tipos de infraestrutura, dominar equipamentos especializados e enfrentar (ou evitar) as criaturas sobrenaturais que vagam pelo mundo fragmentado. Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii | PS5, PS4 Uma nova lenda começa quando você assume o papel de Goro Majima, um homem que perdeu a memória e se reinventa como um pirata em alto-mar. Embarque em uma aventura pirata intensa e moderna com um ex-yakuza que virou capitão pirata e sua tripulação, enquanto eles travam combates eletrizantes em terra e no mar em busca de memórias perdidas e de um tesouro lendário. Atomfall, um jogo de ação e sobrevivência inspirado em fatos reais, se passa cinco anos após o acidente nuclear de Windscale, no norte da Inglaterra. Explore a área de quarentena fictícia, procure suprimentos, crie itens, negocie, lute e use a lábia para sobreviver em um cenário no interior da Inglaterra repleto de personagens bizarros, misticismo, seitas e agências governamentais clandestinas. Produzido por Rebellion, o estúdio por trás de Sniper Elite e Zombie Army, Atomfall desafiará você a desvendar o sombrio mistério do que realmente aconteceu. Uma releitura impressionante da aclamada obra-prima de RPG e o início narrativo da Trilogia Erdrick. Há muitos anos, o grande herói Ortega despediu-se da esposa e do filho ao partir em uma jornada para derrotar o vilão Baramos, o arquidemônio. Ortega falhou em sua missão, e Baramos ainda ameaça o mundo. Agora, ao completar 16 anos, o único filho de Ortega é convocado pelo rei de Aliahan e recebe uma missão da mais alta importância: assumir a jornada de Ortega, derrotar Baramos e salvar o mundo. Em Trepang2, você assume o papel de um soldado fugitivo que não tem lembranças de sua vida anterior, mas possui habilidades sobrenaturais. A vingança não sai da sua cabeça, e você não medirá esforços para conseguir o que quer. Desfira golpes devastadores, esconda-se nas sombras, empunhe armas explosivas e faça os vilões provarem do próprio veneno. Revide, descubra a verdade e enfrente uma ameaça ainda mais mortal do que você. Vivencie toda a intensidade do Campeonato de MotoGP de 2026 com todos os pilotos, equipes, motos e circuitos oficiais de forma mais autêntica: pela primeira vez, os resultados do mundo real atualizam dinamicamente as classificações dos pilotos, influenciando diretamente o desempenho no jogo ao longo da temporada. Destaque-se e acompanhe sua jornada com cartões colecionáveis deslumbrantes que celebram seu progresso. Junte-se à experiência em constante expansão de Hell Let Loose: um jogo de tiro em primeira pessoa hardcore ambientado na Segunda Guerra Mundial, com batalhas épicas de 100 jogadores que envolvem infantaria, tanques, artilharia, uma linha de frente em constante mudança e um metajogo original baseado em recursos, inspirado em jogos de estratégia em tempo real (RTS). Entre na batalha em partidas de vários jogadores de 50 vs. 50 em mapas enormes. Escolha uma das 14 missões na infantaria, os tipos de unidades de reconhecimento e armadura, cada uma equipada com armas, veículos e equipamentos diferentes. Jogue como oficial, batedor, artilheiro, médico, engenheiro, comandante de tanque e muito mais para vivenciar todos os aspectos dos combates da Segunda Guerra Mundial. Cricket 26 – The Official Game of the Ashes | PS5, PS4 Com a novíssima carreira de gestão, uma equipe profissional maior e melhor, o modo Ashes mais completo e um maior controle dentro e fora de campo, graças à gameplay aprimorada e às estratégias detalhadas, o Cricket 26 apresenta u confronto épico. Soul Reaver 2 | PS5, PS4 Nesta sequência do aclamado Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver, assuma novamente o papel de Raziel e lute para voltar, atravessando as areias do tempo, às épocas decisivas e perigosas do passado de Nosgoth em sua busca implacável por Kain. Enfrente novos inimigos enquanto desvenda os mistérios das antigas civilizações de Nosgoth e revele os planos que estão por trás da corrupção dos Pilares. Em um futuro distante, onde todos os recursos da Terra se esgotaram, estar vivo já é um pecado por si só. Condenado a uma pena de prisão de um milhão de anos, você precisa sobreviver a missões letais para ter qualquer esperança de liberdade. Morra na prisão ou viva no combate. A escolha é sua. Use Thorn, sua arma mais confiável, para dominar o campo de batalha. Lute ao lado de aliados e do Acessório, seu ciborgue guardião, para enfrentar inimigos poderosos. *O Catálogo de Jogos PlayStation Plus e os títulos para PlayStation Plus Deluxe podem variar de acordo com a região. Confira na PlayStation Store o dia do lançamento. Os jogos digitais para PS5 disponíveis para streaming da sua biblioteca variam de acordo com o tempo, a região e o país.

sources.title: Side Effects Guaranteed in the First DLC For The Outer Worlds 2, Coming December 2
sources.text: A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation. All signs point to foul play, especially the puddle of what was most likely a person. You recover a video message left by the captain of the vessel, who explains that the crew has been contaminated with something while on a heist that will cause explosive cell death unless they find a cure. And by explosive cell death, she means more like a… “liquefaction”. By the looks of the puddle on the floor: liquefaction indeed. The stakes are set for the release of the first of a two-part narrative DLC expansion of The Outer Worlds 2 on December 2. In Side Effects Guaranteed , the video message you found leads you to Gordon Hazen, one of the leading agents in Sub Rosa, a criminal organization made up of like-minded individuals who have chosen to live their lives stealing from the various factions instead of working for them. Gordon in turn sends you to Elysium Valley, a new region on Eden that is home to a settlement of former Protectorate subjects that have been forgotten by their Protectorate leaders. He believes they may have the answers to saving his crew. He personally favors diplomacy over violence but needs you to do whatever you need to in order to get the information he needs. But Gordon isn’t the only one with interest in Elysium Valley. Another Sub Rosa agent, Algernon Lankester, wants to recruit you to help him exploit the subjects for his own personal gain. The fate of the subjects, the frozen Sub Rosa agents, and the future of Sub Rosa itself is up for you, our intrepid Commander, to decide. A new narrative story is not all that will be coming when Side Effects Guaranteed launches in a few weeks, however. Along with the new region of Elysium Valley to explore, players will encounter new threats like vicious canids and primal sprats. What’s a primal sprat? Just a normal sprat, but about 100 times the size. Surely, they’re just as friendly and forgiving of all the time you “accidentally” shot their much smaller cousins while exploring Arcadia. With these new threats comes the ability to make your Commander even stronger and, of course, more flawed (but in a good way). The level cap will increase from 30 to 36, bringing more skill points to broaden your build. Being able to go to level 36 also means there are three more perks you can acquire, with 15 brand new perks being added into the mix. Four new flaws will also be introduced that can change how your Commander plays, like “Lethally Tolerant,” a flaw that recognizes your built-up resistance to chemicals so your max toxicity will increase. This is great in the moment, but if you ever experience a Toxicity Crash, you will die instantly. Another example is “Must Have Been the Wind,” which will mark an “assassination target” for a combat group. Killing the target will grant a 20% damage and speed buff until the combat ends, but failing to do so or attacking someone who isn’t the target applies a 10% damage and speed debuff to the player for 30 seconds. Truly rewards that come with great risks. Side Effects Guaranteed will also see new weapons, new armors, and new outfits for each of the companions, as well as a brand-new Sub Rosa-run radio station featuring 20 new songs for the game. For those who want to jump straight to the action in the DLC, a new alternate starting point is being added to the main menu when you choose a new game that will allow you to start with a custom save that lands you at the start of the DLC. Start the game, allot your skill and perk points, and enjoy Side Effects Guaranteed right away! This jam-packed adventure with a deep story and systems to build your ideal commander will set up the next DLC for The Outer Worlds 2 that will be coming in Spring of 2027, and choices made will directly impact the next DLC. Part one of this overarching expansion story, Side Effects Guaranteed , will release on December 2 for $14.99, or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2 .

sources.text: Despite Obsidian layoffs, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting two expansions A story expansion for The Outer Worlds 2 has been announced, coming December 2. Side Effects Guaranteed is the first major DLC for The Outer Worlds 2 since its release last October. It will include new story content, as well as new gameplay mechanics, cosmetics, and more. “Side Effects Guaranteed is the first chapter of a two-part expansion for The Outer Worlds 2,” the announcement reads. “A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the shipâs crew in suspended animation to keep themselves alive, as theyâve been infected with something that causes explosive cell death. The hunt for a cure leads to Elysium Valley, a brand-new region on Eden. “Two Sub Rosa agents have very different plans for saving or sacrificing the crew which involve a Protectorate settlement and the future of Sub Rosa, and they want your help. The fate of [the] settlement, the crew, and Sub Rosa itself are yours to decide.” Decisions made in this DLC will carry over into the next one, which is scheduled for Spring 2027. This expansion launches after widespread layoffs across Xbox -owned studios saw a reported 52 job losses at Obsidian . It also saw Obsidian merge with Bethesda , and seemingly go all-in on a new Fallout game . This left the future of Obsidian’s own IP, like The Outer Worlds and Pillars of Eternity, uncertain. Although it now seems that Xbox has allowed Obsidian to finish its post-launch work on The Outer Worlds 2, rather than abandon it entirely. Among the new features introduced in this DLC, there’s a new area, a higher level cap of 36, new flaws and perks, new armour and weapons, and a new radio station. It isn’t clear when in the game the DLC will kick in, but there will be an “alternative start” option when you make a new game, letting you jump straight into the DLC. The Outer Worlds 2: Side Effects Guaranteed releases on December 2 and is priced at $14.99.

Dois agentes da Sub Rosa têm planos bastante diferentes para salvar ou sacrificar a tripulação. Suas propostas envolvem um assentamento do Protetorado e o futuro da própria Sub Rosa, e ambos querem sua ajuda. O destino do assentamento, da tripulação e da Sub Rosa estará em suas mãos. (Os efeitos colaterais podem variar.) Side Effects Guaranteed poderá ser adquirido de forma independente ou através do upgrade para a edição Premium do jogo base, que dá acesso a expansão. O conteúdo adicional também estará disponível para assinantes do serviço Game Pass. The Outer Worlds 2 já está disponível, para PlayStation 5, Xbox Series e PC (via Steam e Microsoft Store ).

sources.title: Anticipated Warhammer 40K tactical RPG Dark Heresy gets a release date
sources.text: Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review . Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure. There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch. Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect . That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider , and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5 .
